page0.text: Hmm, I guess I'll go talk to Saber.

page1.text:
"My favorite food, you said?"
I nod.

page2.text:
Even though I came to the dojo, my body is still numb.
I can't spar with Saber, and I don't feel like talking about the serious things going on right now, so I ask her about her preferences for future reference.
Really, I just want to get to know her.

page3.text: "...You ask strange questions. I do not understand, is there some important meaning in this...?"

page4.text:
"Huh? No, nothing important. You're not a picky eater, so I just got worried about whether you enjoy my food or not.
If I know what food you like, I can avoid the food you dislike."

page5.text:
"...Hm. Then you are mistaken, Shirou. There are no problems with the meals you prepare.
I am satisfied, and I do not think this is possible, but if you were to make a mistake, I do not think I would dislike it even then."

page6.text:
Saber completely changes and watches seriously.
...Well, I can tell that Saber enjoys my food, so I'm glad to hear that. But...

page7.text: "Yeah, but you won't like it if I make something you can't stand in the first place, right? I want you to enjoy the meal, so I want to know what you find dull."

page8.text:
"...Hmm. Dull, you say? Why do you need to know such a thing?"
"So that I can keep it in mind for future reference. I don't think you have any allergies, but it doesn't hurt to ask."

page9.text: "...Hmmm. I'm not convinced, but would answering you improve the quality of your meals in the future...?"

page10.text:
"It will. If your preferences are clear, it'll be easier to put together a menu. I'm sure it'll taste better as well."
"...Then I will cooperate, Master. Please ask away."
Saber sits up straight politely.

page11.text:
"...Hmm."
...I feel like she's pumped up like she's about to start a match.

page12.text:
"Please, Shirou. I am ready."
She urges me on.
...This is an unexpected turn of events, but I also sit up straight.

page13.text:
"Then I'll start off broadly. Do you dislike sweet stuff?"
"I have no problem with it. In fact, I rather like it."
"Okay. Then, what about spicy stuff?"
"I have no problem with that either. I appreciate the stimulation after a workout."

page14.text: "I see, I see. So you're okay with both sweet and spicy. Then, more specifically, are you okay with vegetables?"

page15.text:
"Yes, they are fine. I am not a vegetarian, but ripe vegetables are a must for every meal."
"Hmm. Then what about meat? Chicken, pork, beef...tell me if there's something you don't like. Also, let me know if there's a certain cooking method you like."

page16.text:
"My requirements are few on the matter. Meat is the main character of the meal.
Everything you have made is rather delicious, so I would like for you to cook freely."

page17.text:
"O-oh really? ...This is a bit off topic, but what were the meals like where you're from?"
"..."
Hey.
What's with the face? Why do you have to think it over?

page18.text: "...Err, well. How about you just say whether it was good or bad?"

page19.text:
"...It was slop."
She's muttering.
An opinion full of hatred.
It's so unlike Saber to be so openly negative. With it comes what feels like a flood of dissatisfaction with the incompetence of an individual and the self-hatred of not being able to correct them.

page20.text:
"I-I see. Um...I'm sorry.
Let's get back to the original topic. What about seafood? I've cooked a lot of fish, but you haven't had any shellfish yet, right?"

page21.text: "That is true. I have not had much, but seafood is good for the body. If I disregard the labor required for preparation, it would be one of my favorite foods."

page22.text:
...Okay.
She likes both sweet and spicy, and is fine with vegetables, meat, and fish.

page23.text:
"...I think I've gone about this wrong. Saber, do you have any food you don't like?"
"No, you do not need to worry about that, Shirou. I do not have any foods I dislike."

page24.text:
...Well...
I don't want to say this after asking so much, but I'm starting to feel like these questions were meaningless.

page25.text:
"I see, I see. So, okay. You can eat anything then?"
"Yes. I will eat anything as long as it tastes good.
I am happy to say that not even my palate is dull."
Saber puffs a little with pride.

page26.text:
...
...So then...
I was able to learn one thing from these questions, at least.

page27.text: ...That, well, if I get lazy and put in less effort into making meals, I'm not sure how Saber'll react.
